newsitem.title: ITALY: Ambroveneto has no overstaffing problem.
newsitem.headline: Ambroveneto has no overstaffing problem.

text.p: Italian banking group Ambroveneto said on Tuesday that it does not have a problem of overstaffing and it would cut jobs only as a last resort.

The group's managing director Corrado Passera told the group's annual shareholders meeting that the crisis in Italy's national banking system is structural and will get worse with time, but to cut personnel costs is not sufficient as the industry also needs to cut other costs and raise income.
"Ambroveneto does not have a problem with overstaffing," said Passera, and added that the bank would only touch staff numbers in the final resort.
Banking analysts say the Italian banking system, with nearly 1,000 different banking groups, needs to cut around 30,000 jobs to become competitive with the rest of Europe.
